phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Symbolic execution reveals that while a TOCTOU mutation window exists in the code structure, the KZG cryptographic binding creates an insurmountable constraint that prevents exploitation. The proof P = KZG_Prove(blob, C) cryptographically binds the blob content to the commitment at computation time. Any mutation blob' ≠ blob after this point will cause VerifyBlobKZGProof(blob', C, P) to fail with overwhelming probability (cryptographic security ~2^128). The symbolic path exploration confirms no valid counterexample exists where a mutation passes verification.

path_1_honest_execution.description: Normal honest proposer flow - no mutations

symbolic_variables.blob_i: []byte (131072 bytes) - attacker cannot control directly (from EL)
symbolic_variables.proof_i: []byte (48 bytes) - from req.GetDeneb().KzgProofs or req.GetElectra().KzgProofs or req.GetFulu().KzgProofs

path_constraints: PC1: rawBlobs, proofs ← blobsAndProofs(req) extracts references from protobuf
PC2: blobSidecars ← BuildBlobSidecars(block, rawBlobs, proofs) constructs sidecars
PC3: sidecars[i].Blob = rawBlobs[i] (reference assignment, no copy)
PC7: ROBlob ← NewROBlobWithRoot(sc, root) wraps sidecar
PC8: VerifyBlobKZGProof(blob, commitment, proof) called in verification
PC9: Cryptographic constraint: KZG_Verify(blob, C, P) = 1 ⟺ P was generated via KZG_Prove(blob, C)
path_1_honest_execution.symbolic_outcome: PASS - blob content matches proof, verification succeeds

path_2_mutation_attempt_blob_content.description: Attacker attempts to mutate blob content after sidecar construction

attack_symbolic_state.precondition: Malicious proposer controls ProposeBeaconBlock execution context
attack_symbolic_state.unchanged: sidecars[i].KzgCommitment = C_original, sidecars[i].KzgProof = P_original where P_original = KZG_Prove(original_blob, C_original)

symbolic_constraints: SC1: Let original_blob = blobs[i] at time T_build
SC2: Let P = proofs[i] where P was computed as KZG_Prove(original_blob, C)
SC3: Attacker performs: sidecars[i].Blob ← malicious_blob at time T_mutate (where T_build < T_mutate < T_broadcast)
SC4: Broadcast sends (malicious_blob, C, P) to network
SC5: Receiver executes: result ← KZG_Verify(malicious_blob, C, P)
SC6: Cryptographic security property: Pr[KZG_Verify(blob', C, P) = 1 | P = KZG_Prove(blob, C) ∧ blob' ≠ blob] ≤ 2^-128

path_condition_solving.goal: Find malicious_blob such that KZG_Verify(malicious_blob, C_original, P_original) = 1
path_condition_solving.solver_result: UNSAT - No satisfying assignment exists under computational hardness assumptions
path_condition_solving.reasoning: The KZG commitment scheme is computationally binding. Given a commitment C and proof P that binds to blob, finding a different blob' that verifies with the same (C, P) requires breaking the discrete logarithm problem in the BLS12-381 elliptic curve group, with security level ~128 bits.

path_2_mutation_attempt_blob_content.symbolic_outcome: FAIL - verification rejects mutated blob with overwhelming probability

path_3_mutation_attempt_commitment.description: Attacker attempts to mutate KZG commitment after sidecar construction

attack_symbolic_state.unchanged: sidecars[i].Blob = blob_original, sidecars[i].KzgProof = P_original, sidecars[i].CommitmentInclusionProof = I_original

symbolic_constraints: SC1: I_original = MerkleProof(body_root, C_original, index) - proves C_original ∈ block.body at position index
SC2: Attacker sets: sidecars[i].KzgCommitment ← C_malicious
SC3: Broadcast sends sidecar with (blob, C_malicious, P, I_original)
SC4: Receiver first checks: VerifyKZGInclusionProof(sidecar) which verifies Merkle proof I_original proves C_malicious ∈ block.body
SC5: I_original proves C_original but receiver checks if it proves C_malicious

path_condition_solving.goal: Have VerifyKZGInclusionProof pass with (C_malicious, I_original, block.body)
constraint_system: VerifyMerkleProof(I_original, body_root, C_malicious, index) must return true
path_condition_solving.solver_result: UNSAT - Merkle proof cryptographically binds specific commitment to specific position
path_condition_solving.reasoning: The Merkle inclusion proof I is a hash chain that cryptographically binds C_original to its position in the Merkle tree with root body_root. Changing C to C_malicious breaks the hash chain: Hash(...Hash(C_malicious)...) ≠ body_root. Finding a collision requires breaking SHA-256.

path_3_mutation_attempt_commitment.symbolic_outcome: FAIL - inclusion proof verification rejects swapped commitment

path_4_mutation_attempt_proof.description: Attacker attempts to mutate KZG proof to match mutated blob

attack_symbolic_state.precondition: Malicious proposer mutates blob and attempts to recompute valid proof
attack_symbolic_state.mutation: sidecars[i].Blob = blob_malicious, sidecars[i].KzgProof = P_new where P_new = KZG_Prove(blob_malicious, C_original)

symbolic_constraints: SC1: C_original is committed in block.body (proven by I_original)
SC2: Attacker computes P_new = KZG_Prove(blob_malicious, C_original)
SC3: For KZG_Verify(blob_malicious, C_original, P_new) = 1, we need C_original = BlobToKZGCommitment(blob_malicious)
SC4: But C_original was computed from original_blob: C_original = BlobToKZGCommitment(original_blob)
SC5: Block body contains C_original which is already signed and committed

path_condition_solving.goal: Find blob_malicious such that BlobToKZGCommitment(blob_malicious) = C_original = BlobToKZGCommitment(original_blob)
constraint_system: C_original = BlobToKZGCommitment(original_blob) - fixed in signed block
C_target = C_original - required for valid proof
path_condition_solving.solver_result: UNSAT - Commitment scheme is cryptographically binding
path_condition_solving.reasoning: Finding two different blobs that produce the same KZG commitment requires breaking the computational binding property of KZG commitments, equivalent to solving discrete log in BLS12-381 (128-bit security). This is computationally infeasible.

path_4_mutation_attempt_proof.symbolic_outcome: FAIL - Cannot create valid proof for mutated blob with fixed commitment

path_5_data_column_cell_mutation.description: Attacker attempts to mutate data column cells after construction (Fulu fork)

attack_symbolic_state.precondition: Fulu fork active, proposer creates data columns from blobs

symbolic_constraints: SC1: Original flow: cells, cell_proofs = ComputeCells(blob)
SC2: cell_proofs[col] = KZG_Prove_Cell(blob, col) - binds specific cell to column position
SC3: dataColumn.Column[i] = cells[i][col] for blob i, column col
SC4: Attacker mutates: dataColumn.Column[j] ← malicious_cell
SC5: Verification: VerifyCellKZGProofBatch(commitments[], indices[], cells[], proofs[])
SC6: Batch verification checks: ∀i: KZG_Verify_Cell(commitments[i], indices[i], cells[i], proofs[i]) = 1

path_condition_solving.goal: Have VerifyCellKZGProofBatch pass with mutated cell
constraint_system: proof_j = KZG_Prove_Cell(original_blob_j, col) - fixed at construction
KZG_Verify_Cell(commitment_j, col, cell_mutated, proof_j) must return true
path_condition_solving.solver_result: UNSAT - Cell KZG proof cryptographically binds cell content
path_condition_solving.reasoning: Cell KZG proofs have the same cryptographic binding properties as blob KZG proofs. The proof was computed for the original cell derived from the original blob. Changing the cell breaks the cryptographic relationship between proof, commitment, and cell data.

path_5_data_column_cell_mutation.symbolic_outcome: FAIL - batch verification rejects mutated cells

cryptographic_barrier_analysis.security_property: KZG commitment scheme binding and soundness
cryptographic_barrier_analysis.hardness_assumption: Discrete Logarithm Problem in BLS12-381 elliptic curve group
cryptographic_barrier_analysis.why_toctou_doesnt_matter: While the code allows mutable references to blob/commitment/proof data throughout the construction → broadcast → verification pipeline (creating a TOCTOU window in the traditional sense), the cryptographic properties of KZG commitments create an implicit immutability guarantee. Any mutation that changes blob content, commitment, or their binding invalidates the cryptographic proof relationship. The verification step acts as a cryptographic integrity check that detects any mutation with overwhelming probability (failure rate ≤ 2^-128). Therefore, the mutation window exists in the code structure but is cryptographically unexploitable.
cryptographic_barrier_analysis.code_vs_crypto_security: The codebase relies on cryptographic security rather than memory safety. The 'read-only' wrappers (ROBlob, RODataColumn) are naming conventions, not enforcement mechanisms - the underlying protobuf data remains mutable. However, this implementation choice is acceptable because the KZG verification provides stronger security than language-level immutability could achieve. Even if an attacker had arbitrary memory write access to mutate sidecar fields, they cannot produce a mutation that passes cryptographic verification.

edge_cases_analyzed.symbolic_outcome: KZG verification detects mismatch and rejects sidecar
edge_cases_analyzed.note: Even though ELMemPoolRequirements = [] (no verification on EL data), the subsequent gossip/sync verification will catch invalid proofs

edge_cases_analyzed.symbolic_outcome: Data race possible but verification still catches any corrupted data
edge_cases_analyzed.note: Concurrent modification might cause undefined behavior but cannot produce a valid but malicious sidecar

edge_cases_analyzed.symbolic_outcome: References might change but content is verified post-unmarshaling
edge_cases_analyzed.note: Verification happens after unmarshaling on receiver side with fresh data

theoretical_vs_practical.theoretical_vulnerability: TOCTOU mutation window exists in code structure
theoretical_vs_practical.quantum_resistance: BLS12-381 vulnerable to Shor's algorithm (quantum computers), but this affects all Ethereum consensus, not specific to this TOCTOU issue

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The mutation window is reachable by a malicious proposer who controls the ProposeBeaconBlock execution context. However, reachability analysis confirms that while an attacker can reach the mutation point (between sidecar construction and broadcast), all attempted mutations are cryptographically detected and rejected during verification. The attack surface exists but is cryptographically protected rather than being unreachable or prevented by input validation.

entry_points.name: ProposeBeaconBlock gRPC endpoint
entry_points.control_level: Full control over GenericSignedBeaconBlock contents if attacker is the block proposer
preconditions: Attacker must be selected as the proposer for a specific slot
Attacker must have validator key to sign the block
Beacon node accepts the signed block from attacker's validator client
attacker_capabilities: Control blob content in req.GetDeneb().Blobs / req.GetElectra().Blobs / req.GetFulu().Blobs
Control proof content in req.GetDeneb().KzgProofs / req.GetElectra().KzgProofs / req.GetFulu().KzgProofs
Control block.body.BlobKzgCommitments (but these must match proofs for block to be valid)
Modify sidecar fields after construction if attacker controls the server process (insider threat)

entry_points.name: Execution Layer BlobsBundle via getPayload
preconditions: Attacker must compromise the execution layer client (e.g., Geth, Nethermind)
EL must provide malicious blobs/proofs in BlobsBundle response
entry_points.note: ELMemPoolRequirements = [] means no immediate verification, but gossip verification will catch invalid data

detailed_flow: STEP 1: Attacker-controlled data enters via req.GetDeneb().Blobs[] / req.GetElectra().Blobs[] / req.GetFulu().Blobs[] or from EL BlobsBundle
STEP 2: blobsAndProofs(req) extracts blobs[] and proofs[] as [][]byte slices (references, not copies)
STEP 3: BuildBlobSidecars(block, blobs, proofs) creates sidecars with fields pointing to these slices
- sidecars[i].Blob = blobs[i] (reference assignment)
- sidecars[i].KzgCommitment = block.body.BlobKzgCommitments[i] (reference)
- sidecars[i].KzgProof = proofs[i] (reference)
- sidecars[i].CommitmentInclusionProof = MerkleProof(block.body, i) (newly computed)
STEP 4: [MUTATION WINDOW] Between BuildBlobSidecars() return and broadcastAndReceiveBlobs() call
- Attacker could hypothetically modify sidecars[i].Blob, sidecars[i].KzgCommitment, or sidecars[i].KzgProof
- In normal flow this doesn't happen, but code structure allows it (mutable references)
STEP 5: broadcastAndReceiveBlobs(ctx, sidecars, root) broadcasts each sidecar
- For each sidecar: P2P.BroadcastBlob(ctx, index, sidecar)
- Protobuf marshaling occurs but doesn't prevent prior mutation
STEP 6: Self-receive path: blocks.NewROBlobWithRoot(sidecar, root) wraps sidecar
- ROBlob wrapper provides no actual immutability (just wraps pointer)
- blocks.NewVerifiedROBlob(readOnlySc) upgrades WITHOUT verification (proposer trusts self)
STEP 7: Network receivers get sidecars and perform full verification
- ROBlobVerifier.SidecarInclusionProven() verifies Merkle proof
- ROBlobVerifier.SidecarKzgProofVerified() calls Verify(blobSidecars...)
- kzg/validation.go:29-48: VerifyBlobKZGProof(blob, commitment, proof)
- Cryptographic check detects any mutation

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attacker_control_scope: Malicious proposer can control input data (blobs, proofs, commitments) and potentially modify sidecar fields if they compromise the beacon node process, but cannot make invalid data pass cryptographic verification
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.classification_rationale: The vulnerability is NOT unreachable - a malicious proposer can reach the mutation point and attempt to exploit the TOCTOU window. However, the exploitation is prevented by defense-in-depth through cryptographic verification layers. While the code structure has a weakness (mutable references, no defensive copying), the cryptographic properties of KZG commitments provide a second line of defense that makes exploitation computationally infeasible. This is a case where the codebase relies on cryptographic security to compensate for unsafe memory handling practices.
notes: CRITICAL INSIGHT: This is a defense-in-depth scenario, NOT an unreachable or internally-safe scenario. The mutation window is reachable, but cryptographic verification provides robust protection.

The 'self-receive' path is VULNERABLE to accepting invalid data from malicious proposer: broadcastAndReceiveBlobs() creates VerifiedROBlob via blocks.NewVerifiedROBlob(readOnlySc) WITHOUT running verification (proposer.go:493). This means the proposer's own node will accept mutated sidecars. However, network peers perform full verification, so the attack fails at the network level.

ELMemPoolRequirements being empty (blob.go:59) is a design choice reflecting trust in the execution layer. However, this creates a trust boundary violation - if EL is compromised, it can provide invalid blobs/proofs that won't be caught until gossip/sync verification. This is a separate issue from the TOCTOU window.

The code would benefit from defensive improvements even though cryptographic security prevents exploitation: (1) Deep copy blob/commitment/proof data in BuildBlobSidecars(), (2) Add EL mempool verification requirements, (3) Use immutable data structures or const pointers, (4) Add integrity hash check before broadcast. However, these are defense-in-depth hardening, not critical security fixes.

Quantum computing threat: If/when large-scale quantum computers exist, they could break BLS12-381 discrete log using Shor's algorithm, which would compromise all KZG proofs including this verification layer. However, this affects the entire Ethereum consensus layer, not just this specific code path.

From an attacker's perspective: The most viable attack vector is compromising the execution layer to provide invalid blobs/proofs, then relying on the empty ELMemPoolRequirements to skip immediate verification. But gossip verification will still catch this, so the attack window is limited to the proposer's own node accepting invalid data.
